deities: Sri Krishna (Parthasarathi form, holding a whip in the right hand and a conch in the left)
Sub-deities in the complex (per Kerala temple tradition)
festivals: Aaraattu festival (10 days, March-April; flag hosting on Atham day of Meenam, main day on Thiruvonam; elephant procession, Panchavadyam, Velakali and fireworks)
Chambakulam Moolam (boat race on the Moolam day of Midhunam, June-July, commemorating the bringing of the Krishna idol)
Pallipana (rare ritual conducted once every 12 years)

history.period: 15th-17th century CE (built by Chembakasserry ruler Pooradam Thirunal Devanarayanan Thampuran)
history.summary: The Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple was built by the local ruler Chembakasserry Pooradam Thirunal Devanarayanan Thampuran, an ardent devotee of Krishna. Legend says the king and the saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar were travelling along the backwaters when they heard the sound of a flute from a peepul tree; the saint had a vision of Krishna playing his flute, and the king built the temple where the vision appeared, bringing the idol from the Karinkulam temple in Kurichi near Kottayam. The idol is in the Parthasarathi (charioteer) form of Krishna, holding a whip in the right hand and a conch in the left. The temple is deeply linked with Guruvayoor: during Tipu Sultan's raids in 1789 the Guruvayoor idol was brought to Ambalappuzha for safekeeping, and devotees believe Guruvayoorappan comes here daily at the time of the Palpayasam nivedyam. It is counted among the seven greatest temples of Travancore and as one of the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnavite tradition. The famous Ambalappuzha Palpayasam (sweet rice-and-milk porridge) originates from the legend of Krishna, disguised as a sage, defeating the king at chess and demanding rice grains doubled on each of the 64 squares - the king was then told to serve palpayasam to pilgrims daily until the debt was repaid. The traditional art form Ottan Thullal was first performed here by its creator, the poet Kunchan Nambiar.

name: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple
town_description: Ambalappuzha is a coastal temple town about 14 km south of Alappuzha in Kerala's backwater region, on the Alappuzha-Kollam highway. Its name is said to mean 'temple river' in Malayalam, a reference to the Pampa river nearby; before it was called Ambalappuzha the area was known as Chembakasserry, headquarters of the erstwhile Chembakasseri kingdom. The town is a well-known Hindu pilgrim centre centred on the Sri Krishna temple, and lies close to Alappuzha's houseboat backwaters and the Chambakulam waterway.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 64-85 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Ambalappuzha station (approx. 2 km); Alappuzha Junction (approx. 14 km), well connected across Kerala.
travel.road: About 14 km south of Alappuzha on the Alappuzha-Kollam highway (SH 12); regular KSRTC and private buses, autos and taxis run between Alappuzha and Ambalappuzha. The temple is about 1.5 km east of the Ambalappuzha town junction.

visitor_information.best_time: September to March for pleasant weather. The Aaraattu festival (March-April) and Chambakulam Moolam (June-July) are the most vibrant times to visit; early mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 3:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM, closed 12:00 noon to 5:00 PM (verify — minor variations exist between sources). Free darshan. Men must remove shirts before entering, per Kerala temple tradition. Palpayasam requires a token before noon; distribution after the midday Uchha Pooja; approx. Rs. 80 for half a litre, Rs. 160 for one litre.
